headline: Data Centers Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of new energy infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy users like data centers, aiming to decrease household utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, Senator Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Senator Scott Surovell, Dominion Energy (with amendments)
opponents: Data Center Coalition (initially concerned about language)
news_headline: Virginia Budget Creates New Electricity Consumption Tax for Data Centers
news_summary: Virginia's new budget includes a first-ever electricity consumption tax on data centers, effective July 1, 2026, to ensure they pay their fair share for energy use. This measure aims to prevent data centers from driving up costs for Virginia families, with projections of up to $600 million annually in revenue.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water suppliers report data center water consumption to the state, increasing transparency for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, conservation groups, environmental advocates
opponents: Data center industry (initially, due to perceived singling out)
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality. This transparency measure aims to provide credible numbers on water consumption, aggregated and compared to other industries, to aid in water supply planning.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires impact assessments for new data centers regarding noise and other environmental factors, giving localities more control over their siting.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Del. Josh Thomas, residents near data centers, environmental groups, Governor Abigail Spanberger
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as these are new regulations)
news_headline: Virginia Budget Mandates Data Center Noise Regulations
news_summary: Virginia's new budget includes provisions from HB 153, requiring environmental sound assessments for new data centers and mandating the DEQ to establish strict noise regulations by 2029. This addresses growing concerns from residents about noise pollution from data center facilities.
